title: Quillen B: a comma category models the homotopy fiber
statement:
Use small categories, ordinary nerves, geometric realization, Kan complexes and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Write $R(K)=\operatorname{Sing}(|K|)$, where $\operatorname{Sing}(T)_n=\operatorname{Cont}(|\Delta^n|,T)$ with precomposition operators; use the natural characteristic-map unit $K\to R(K)$. Let $U:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a functor between small categories. For each $b$, let $(U\downarrow b)$ have objects $(e,\alpha:Ue\to b)$ and arrows $h:e\to e'$ satisfying $\alpha'U(h)=\alpha$. Suppose every $\beta:b_0\to b_1$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence $N(U\downarrow b_0)\to N(U\downarrow b_1)$ by postcomposition. Then the canonical map
$$c_{U,b}:R N(U\downarrow b)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{b}(RNU)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The vertex $b$ on the right is the constant singular simplex at the nerve vertex $b$. The map is induced by the forgetful functor $(U\downarrow b)\to\mathcal E$ and the natural transformation from its composite with $U$ to the constant functor at $b$: realize this transformation, apply $\operatorname{Sing}$, and restrict the singular interval along $\Delta^1\to\operatorname{Sing}([0,1])$. Here the homotopy fiber uses the path-space model of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The comparison is natural for strictly commuting squares $GU=U'F$ of functors and specified objects $b\in\mathcal B$, $b'=G(b)\in\mathcal B'$: the comma functor is $(e,\alpha)\mapsto(F(e),G(\alpha))$, and the homotopy-fiber map is induced by $RNF$ and $RNG$. Both functors $U,U'$ in this naturality assertion satisfy the stated comma-transition hypothesis. No assumption that the comma categories are contractible is made.
